headline: Inquest Finds Missed Opportunities In Custody Death Of Tammy Shipley
seoTitle: Inquest Into Death Of Tammy Shipley
metaDescription: A coroner's inquest has determined that Tammy Shipley's death in custody could have been prevented had proper monitoring and intervention been provided.
aiSummaryBullets: Tammy Shipley died in prison after consuming approximately 20 litres of water.
A coroner concluded that failure to conduct required welfare checks led to the fatal outcome.
The inquest identified missed opportunities to divert the deceased from the justice system before her imprisonment.
aiContextParagraph: An official inquest has examined the circumstances surrounding the death of Tammy Shipley, an Aboriginal woman who died while held in custody. Findings indicate that the deceased consumed at least 20 litres of water, leading to a collapse that resulted in her death. The coroner determined that prison staff failed to perform mandated, regular health and welfare monitoring of the inmate, which would have allowed them to intervene and stop the excessive water consumption. Furthermore, the inquest highlighted that various systemic opportunities to divert the woman from entering the prison system were overlooked prior to her incarceration. The report serves as a formal review into the internal processes and systemic failures that contributed to this event, emphasizing the necessity of adhering to established safety protocols for incarcerated individuals.
whyItIsViral: The topic has gained attention through coverage from two independent news outlets reflecting on the official findings of the coroner's inquest.
